title: Historical obligation-ledger allowlists refuse the whole state load on any shape they did not anticipate
outcome: A TermAl build without gated control starts on a store that holds gated-era obligation history: every obligation-ledger shape that earlier builds actually wrote is either accepted by the passive historical validators or kept as opaque history, so the state load is never refused for a well-formed historical entry.
acceptance: Evidence that the historical validators (historical_request_shape, historical_queued_shape, historical_decision_card_shape and the transfer/successor matchers in src/engram_session_obligations.rs) accept every obligation shape that the gated builds' writers could produce. Acceptable evidence: a test corpus generated from the BASE writers, OR a validation run against a copy of a real store made under an authorised procedure. Alternatively, a change that keeps unrecognised historical entries as opaque raw history instead of refusing the load, with a test.
A test showing that a store with a gated-era obligation ledger loads, and that a malformed ledger is still refused.

completion.summary: The historical validators accept every ledger shape the gated writers produced in a 4553-ledger corpus, and a malformed ledger is still refused with nothing written. Keeping the corpus on master is w-30ad5d74b7dd.
